subject: SLA exit rights and fixed-sum buyout request
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@acmecloudware.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA exit rights and fixed-sum buyout request

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we dig through procurement and legal review, a few items in your standard SLA are blockers for Acme Cloudware before we can recommend Redwood to the buying committee. High level asks below; I attached our standard SLA requirements (acme_sla_requirements_v3.pdf).

1) Termination / buyout: we require an unconditional, fixed-sum buyout (liquidated damages) option if the service fails to meet the uptime/latency commitments for a sustained period. Specifically, Acme will request an immediate termination right after three separate "severity-1" incidents within a 90-day window, with a fixed buyout equal to six months of committed spend.

2) Fee at risk / escrow: we ask Redwood to place an escrow equal to six months of expected committed fees, payable to Acme if termination criteria are met.

3) Caps and cure: we are open to a short cure period, but the cure window must not exceed 14 days for S1 incidents. Credits alone are insufficient for our compliance team.

We need confirmation that these terms are acceptable or an alternate path that provides equivalent financial protection. Legal will follow up with redlines shortly. We are trying to close procurement by end of quarter.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloudware

Attachment: acme_sla_requirements_v3.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@acmecloudware.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exit rights and fixed-sum buyout request

Jordan —

Appreciate the candid note and the attachment — this is helpful context. We hear three asks: (1) fixed-sum buyout on termination, (2) escrow of six months' fees, (3) short cure windows.

A few quick points from our side:
- Redwood's standard approach has historically been credits + cure windows + a capped cash remediation for extreme cases. Credits are typically preferable because they preserve long-term relationship incentives.
- An unconditional fixed-sum buyout equal to six months' committed spend and a six-month escrow is a large operational and financial burden for us, and could materially affect pricing and availability for other customers.

That said, we're committed to finding a path forward. Would Acme consider an alternative compromise we can propose internally to Finance & Legal? Example proposal we can put on the table:
- Staged buyout ladder rather than an immediate six-month lump sum: e.g., fee-at-risk pool that grows with repeat, uncured incidents (1st sustained S1: 1 month; 2nd within 90 days: 2 months; 3rd: 3 months; capped at 3 months)
- 30-day cure period for S1s with mandatory incident post-mortem and remediation plan; if remediation assertions are not met, funds from an escrowed pool can be released.
- For enterprise accounts with committed annual spend > $X, we can consider a third-party escrow equal to up to 3 months of committed fees, not 6.

If that sounds like something worth discussing, let me know and I can pull Legal into a short call tomorrow. Attached a draft term sheet with the high-level counter (redwood_counter_sla_terms_draft.docx).

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_counter_sla_terms_draft.docx (Word, 42KB)

From: Legal (Acme Cloudware) <legal@acmecloudware.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@acmecloudware.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exit rights and fixed-sum buyout request

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick reply. We reviewed your counter and cannot accept credits-only approaches as a substitute for cash remediation at the enterprise level. Our position:

- Liquidated damages / buyout: firm requirement of six months' committed fees as the buyout sum.
- Escrow: yes, third-party escrow acceptable but must equal six months' committed fees at contract signature.
- Cure: 14 days maximum for S1 incidents.

We attached our redlines to the SLA (Acme_SLA_Redlines.docx). Please confirm whether Redwood has internal approval to accept a 6-month escrow or if you require escalations. Time is sensitive — if we don't have a viable remediation path by 6/10 we will escalate to alternatives.

Regards,
Maria Chen
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloudware

Attachment: Acme_SLA_Redlines.docx (Word, 28KB)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-04T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme SLA redlines — quick internal options

Karthik —

Looping you in with what I'd propose before we push another counter. High-level risk notes for Legal/Finance: Acme's asks (6mo buyout + 6mo escrow) would represent significant cash exposure and set a precedent for other large deals. If we agree programmatically to 6mo escrows we'll have to bake that into T&Cs and pricing.

Suggested compromise bullets to present to Acme:
- Offer a capped buyout / LD equal to three (3) months of committed fees rather than six; for enterprise accounts, this is still meaningful but manageable for Redwood's finance team.
- Escrow only for customers with committed ARR > $1M; escrow amount capped at 3 months' committed fees; for others offer a letter of credit alternative.
- Maintain a 30-day cure period for S1s, but accelerate to 14 days if repeat offenses occur within a 90-day window.
- Include a mutual termination right for cause after repeated uncured incidents, with pro-rata refund of pre-paid fees plus the capped buyout.

If you agree, I'll get Legal to propose language and have Finance run exposure models.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@acmecloudware.com>, Legal (Acme Cloudware) <legal@acmecloudware.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exit rights and fixed-sum buyout request

Jordan / Maria —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. We want to keep this moving toward a signature and appreciate Acme's need for strong financial protections. Redwood can propose the following compromise that we believe balances Acme's risk requirements with Redwood's operational/financial constraints:

1) Staged buyout ladder (fee-at-risk): a 3-step ladder tied to repeat, uncured S1 incidents within a rolling 90-day window. Payouts: 1st sustained S1 (post-cure) = 1 month committed spend; 2nd = 2 months; 3rd (and thereafter) = 3 months, capped at 3 months total.

2) Escrow: for accounts with committed ARR >= $1,000,000 we will place an amount equal to 3 months' committed fees in a third-party escrow at contract signature. For accounts below that threshold, we will accept a letter of credit or a refundable holdback mechanism.

3) Cure and remediation: 30-day cure period for S1s by default. If an S1 recurs within 90 days, the cure window reduces to 14 days for subsequent incidents. Each S1 must include a documented remediation plan and timeline; failure to meet the plan enables escalation to escrow release/fee-at-risk payout.

4) Termination: mutual termination for cause after three uncured S1 incidents within a 90-day window; upon termination, Acme would receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees plus the applicable staged buyout amount (capped at 3 months).

5) Cap and limitation: Redwood proposes a single aggregate cap equal to the committed fees for the 12-month term (i.e., 12 months), to ensure predictable exposure.

Next steps: if Acme is open to this structure we can have our Legal team provide redline language and schedule a 30-minute legal alignment call on Thursday 6/10. I included a brief redline PDF (redwood_sla_compromise_redlines.pdf) and a DocuSign envelope to accelerate once legal aligns.
